lead_raw_text:
The structure of MgV2Ni crystallizes in the hexagonal space group P6_3/mmc (No. 194), with a unit cell containing eight atoms—Mg2V4Ni2—distributed across three independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows Mg and Ni each coordinated by 12 neighbors (6 Ni and 6 V for Mg; 6 Mg and 6 V for Ni), while V has 15 neighbors (6 Mg, 6 Ni, 3 V), all described as close-packed-like local arrangements with distances from 2.50 to 2.88 Å. The geometric neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component spanning all eight sites. Validated polyhedron-sharing analysis reveals Mg–V, Mg–Ni, Ni–V, and V–V 12-, 15-, and 12-vertex coordination polyhedra sharing corners, edges, and faces.
